transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-05 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Omar (Redwood SE), Priya (Halcyon Head of ML), Ethan (Eng Mgr), Sara (Sec/Comp)

Summary: Quick scoping for a 6-week pilot to validate inference economics and integration path. Focus on OpenAI-compatible endpoints, function/tool calling for product catalog ops, structured JSON outputs for fulfillment systems, and benchmarks for latency/throughput. Security and VPC/KMS constraints discussed.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time. Quick intro — I'm Maya, AE on the Halcyon account, and Omar is our SE.
[00:45] Priya: Hi, thanks. I'm Priya, I run ML here. We want to scope a POC to see if Redwood can meet our latency/cost targets for catalog enrichment and conversational storefront.
[01:30] Omar: Cool, high level, what are the success criteria you care about? Latency p95, throughput, cost per 1k tokens, etc?
[02:10] Ethan: Two main things: 1) p95 generation latency under 200ms for short prompts (~150 tokens) for synchronous flows, and 2) sustained throughput of ~120 reqs/sec during peak shopping hours. Cost target is secondary but important — roughly dollar-per-1k target based on current vendor spend.
[03:00] Priya: Also quality thresholds: precision on entity extraction for structured outputs — we need >95% extraction accuracy on key fields (sku, price, availability) for our downstream fulfillment.
[03:45] Sara: And from compliance, we need SOC2 scope, KMS-managed keys for any private deployments, VPC peering or private link for Dedicated, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[04:30] Maya: Great, that helps. Proposed POC: 6 weeks total — 2-week integration & baseline, 2-week benchmark & optimization, 2-week validation with real traffic shadowing. Does that align?
[05:15] Ethan: Sounds reasonable, depends on how quickly we can get sample data and infra access. We have a week to carve out infra windows.
[06:00] Omar: For integration paths, Redwood supports OpenAI-compatible endpoints (chat completions + function calling), plus our native SDKs (python/node) with examples. You can call the /v1/chat/completions-compatible endpoint or use the SDKs for streaming and structured outputs.
[06:45] Priya: We use a node/ts stack for product and python for offline. Examples would be ideal.
[07:30] Omar: We'll send a repo with working python and node examples — short examples: auth, streaming, function/schema definitions, and sample JSON schema enforcement for structured output. Note: function calling behavior is slightly different across models; we'll include recommended hints for Redwood's verified model profiles.
[08:20] Priya: For the structured output, we need canonical JSON with a fixed schema. Can Redwood guarantee that format? We've had hallucinations in past vendors.
[09:00] Omar: We provide a couple layers: 1) model-side schema constraints (function calling + JSON schema in prompt), 2) post-parse validators in SDK that can reject malformed responses, and 3) you can run a quick verification step in the serving runtime to drop outputs that don't match. We'll show an example where the SDK returns a 'schema_valid': false flag when it doesn't validate.
[09:50] Ethan: That helps. How about retries and idempotency? If we're doing transactional updates in our fulfillment system, we need deterministic outputs for retries.
[10:30] Maya: Good point — for transactional flows we recommend adding request-level ids and using 'deterministic' config profiles (lower temperature, sampling off) and pinning model versions. Redwood supports pinned model versions for POCs.
[11:15] Priya: Workload sizing: we estimate 3M tokens/day at peak across chat and completion flows, avg 220 tokens per call, with spikes to 1500 concurrent sessions during promotions. Is that in line with your capacity planning?
[12:00] Omar: That's useful. Rough calc — 3M tokens/day maps to ~35 requests/sec average (depending on token distribution), but your concurrency number matters for the p95 latency target. For 1500 concurrent sessions, if those are synchronous, Dedicated capacity is recommended to hit consistent p95 SLAs. Hosted can work for baseline but may have more variance.
[13:00] Priya: We're open to starting hosted and then moving to Dedicated if the pilot proves out. Cost sensitivity though.
[13:30] Maya: Pilot pricing — we'll propose a hosted baseline + optional reserved dedicated nodes for the benchmark windows. We'll include burst hours pricing.
[14:10] Sara: For security, if we go Dedicated, we need VPC/private link and KMS integration. Do you support HSM-backed keys?
[14:40] Omar: Yes — KMS/HSM integrations in Private/Dedicated modes. For hosted, we recommend envelope encryption; for Dedicated/Private we can integrate your KMS and HSM per our Private offering. We'll attach the security whitepaper.
[15:20] Ethan: Benchmarks — can Redwood run an apples-to-apples throughput and latency benchmark vs our current provider? We'll provide sample prompts and a synthetic traffic profile.
[15:50] Omar: Absolutely. We'll run two benchmark passes: 1) hosted cluster with your typical payloads, and 2) dedicated-reserved instance with pinned model. We'll report p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens. We'll also capture cold-starts and steady-state.
[16:40] Priya: Do you support streaming for partial results? For our UI we want to stream snippets as they arrive.
[17:10] Omar: Yes — streaming via SDK or SSE from OpenAI-compatible endpoint. We'll provide node streaming example and guidance on chunking to keep UI latency low.
[17:50] Priya: For function/tool calling: we want Redwood to call our product catalog enrichment service at inference time to fetch latest stock. Is that feasible?
[18:30] Omar: We have two approaches: 1) use function calling where the model returns a function invocation that your infra executes and returns results back for finalization, or 2) use pre-invocation enrichment where you call your catalog API first and include the fresh data in the prompt. Function calling reduces prompt size but adds a round trip. For tight p95, pre-fetching is often better. We'll show both patterns.
[19:30] Ethan: If function calling adds a round trip, that could blow latency. For the synchronous purchase flow we probably need prefetching. For async background enrichment, function calling is fine.
[20:00] Priya: Regarding structured outputs — can you show a sample JSON schema for product extraction?
[20:30] Omar: Yes, example in repo: {"sku": "string", "price": "float", "availability": "in_stock|out_of_stock"} plus validators. We'll also include a fuzzing harness to estimate failure rates.
[21:10] Maya: Timelines — proposed milestones: Week 0: kick-off + infra access; Week 1-2: integration & smoke runs; Week 3-4: benchmark & optimization; Week 5-6: shadow & validation. Final decision after week 6.
[21:50] Priya: That pace works if we can get credentials and sample prompts this week.
[22:20] Sara: Legal question — data retention for hosted POC: can you limit retention for logs and not use data for model training?
[22:50] Omar: Yes, we have contractual options to turn off data usage for training; logs can be retained for troubleshooting and then auto-expired. For Dedicated/Private, you control retention fully.
[23:30] Ethan: About SDKs — do you support both python and node feature parity for streaming, function calling, and structured output?
[24:00] Omar: Yes, parity is high. Differences are mostly around streaming APIs. We'll provide both example repos and a one-click quickstart for node.
[24:40] Priya: Any gotchas around OpenAI-compatible endpoints? We rely on a small wrapper internally that expects the OpenAI shapes.
[25:10] Omar: Redwood's OpenAI-compatible endpoints mirror the common shapes (messages, functions, streaming) but with added query params for model pins, route hints, and batching settings. If you rely on specific nonstandard fields, we'll map them — but most customers plug them in with minimal changes.
[25:50] Maya: For benchmarks, what models will you recommend for our workloads? Priya, do you prefer open models or redwood-verified weights?
[26:30] Priya: We prefer open models for cost control but quality matters; if Redwood can show quantized variants that meet quality/cost tradeoffs, that's ideal.
[27:00] Omar: We'll propose a matrix: open-1 (quantized) for cost baseline, open-2 (full precision) for quality baseline, and a Redwood-verified tuned model as another data point. We'll surface quantization levels and expected token/sec on your hardware.
[27:45] Ethan: Do you support running benchmarks against our on-prem hardware? We might want Private deployment later.
[28:10] Omar: For Private, yes — we can provide a local benchmark harness and kernel recommendations. For the pilot we'll stick to hosted + dedicated to accelerate.
[28:45] Priya: Observability — we need per-request token-level cost, latency breakdown for decode vs network vs preproc, and tracing hooks.
[29:15] Omar: Redwood Console has per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, and tracing. We'll enable a debug level with request ids forwarded to your SIEM.
[29:50] Sara: For RBAC and SSO, we use SAML and Okta; we need admin roles and audit trails.
[30:20] Maya: Redwood supports SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and role-based access controls. We'll include the admin guide.
[31:00] Ethan: Any limitations around function calling calling external services? Rate limiting?
[31:30] Omar: Function invocation is subject to the same throughput limits; if you use Dedicated you get predictable quotas. We'll model the extra latency introduced by your function endpoint in the benchmark.
[32:00] Priya: For the schema validation step, if the SDK rejects an output, what's the recommended retry logic? Just re-ask with clarifying system prompt?
[32:40] Omar: Recommended pattern: fail-fast to a fallback human review queue for critical flows; for noncritical, re-run with a more constrained prompt (lower temperature + explicit schema enforcement). We'll include templates.
[33:20] Maya: I want to call out success criteria again so we're aligned: 1) p95 <200ms for sync short prompts, 2) throughput 120 reqs/sec sustained during peak, 3) structured extraction >=95% accuracy, 4) compliance checkboxes satisfied (SOC2, KMS integration).
[34:10] Priya: Agreed, those are our gating criteria. If you can show cost parity within 20% of current vendor at same quality, that helps too.
[34:50] Omar: We'll aim to include cost per 1k tokens for each model variant and also an estimated monthly cost for your projected 3M tokens/day.
[35:30] Ethan: On data handling — can you forward logs to our Splunk instance?
[35:50] Omar: Yes — audit logs can be forwarded; we'll include config for forwarding and retention policies.
[36:20] Priya: For development ergonomics, do you provide a local mock server for the OpenAI-compatible API? That would speed initial integration.
[36:50] Omar: Yes, local mock and a sandbox hosted endpoint. The mock returns deterministic responses for CI tests.
[37:20] Sara: Legal again — we'll need a DPA addendum and model usage clause. Who on your side handles that?
[37:50] Maya: I'll loop in our legal ops; we'll send a template DPA and the security pack as part of the next email.
[38:30] Priya: Any notes on model drift monitoring? We'll want regression alerts tied to prompt sets/evals.
[39:00] Omar: Redwood Optimize includes eval hooks and regression alerts; for the pilot we'll set up a small eval suite against your golden prompt set and raise alerts if metrics drop below thresholds.
[39:40] Ethan: For the actual benchmark run, what do you need from us? Prompt templates, sample traffic profile, auth keys?
[40:05] Omar: We'll need: 1) representative prompt set, 2) synthetic traffic profile (concurrency distribution), 3) sample outputs/golden labels for extraction accuracy, and 4) an enablement account for the test runs.
[40:40] Priya: We'll aim to deliver those by 2026-11-11.
[41:10] Maya: Scheduling: Omar, can you own the benchmark plan and run?
[41:30] Omar: Yep, I'll prep the harness and schedule the runs. I'll also include instructions for running the local mock and the node/python quickstarts.
[42:00] Priya: One more question — do you have any recommended prompt patterns to improve schema fidelity without exploding token counts?
[42:30] Omar: Use concise schema hints, constrained vocabulary examples, and prefer function calling when possible. We'll include a short guide with examples and a tradeoff table (latency vs token size vs reliability).
[43:10] Ethan: On rollouts, if pilot succeeds, what's the typical migration path to Dedicated? Is there downtime?
[43:40] Omar: Migration is usually seamless — you can pin traffic to Dedicated routes and gradually cutover with A/B or canary deploys using our routing policies. No major downtime expected.
[44:10] Sara: For auditability, we need immutable request logs for a 90-day window. Is that configurable?
[44:40] Omar: Yes, retention windows are configurable and we can push logs to your retention store.
[45:10] Priya: Anything else from your side?
[45:30] Maya: I'll summarize next steps after the call.
[45:50] Priya: Thanks all.
[46:10] Ethan: Quick tight question — streaming chunk size for node SDK — default?
[46:30] Omar: Default is 256 chars but adjustable; we'll note a recommended chunk size for your UI.
[47:00] Priya: Great.
[47:30] Maya: Alright, recap: Maya sends pricing + SOW, Omar sends benchmark plan + quickstarts, Halcyon shares prompts + data by 11/11, Sara confirms compliance contacts. Schedule benchmark window 11/13-11/16.
[48:10] Priya: Sounds good.
[48:40] Omar: I'll follow up with the harness and a Google sheet to collect metrics.
[49:00] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email.
[51:30] (call ends)

--- End transcript ---
